risks.risk: Hidden faults may exist despite seller’s claim (dead/intermittent keys, button faults, or speaker issues).
risks.proof: Ask for a video: power on with screen visible, then demonstrate at least one full octave of keys with audible sound and press several buttons (including volume and a few function/menu buttons).
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully proven (worst case: treat as needing testing/possible faults).

risks.risk: Display/backlight or menu responsiveness may be damaged/glitchy (wear is visible).
risks.proof: Ask for a close-up video of the screen turning on and navigating menus without freezing/glitching.
risks.if_unproven: Price as display condition uncertain (worst case: assume display may be problematic).

risks.risk: Adapter may be missing or wrong spec, preventing proper testing/usage.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the exact adapter label/spec and the connector end, or a video showing the adapter powering the keyboard.
risks.if_unproven: Price as adapter not guaranteed (worst case: buyer may need to source one).

risks.risk: Crackle/noise may occur only under certain notes, volume levels, or when using speakers/headphones.
risks.proof: Ask for an audio clip: play sustained notes/chords across low/mid/high range, then stop/start to show consistency; include headphone output if possible.
risks.if_unproven: Price as possible crackle/audio noise (worst case: assume crackle may be present).

proof_requests: Power-on video with the screen clearly visible and responsive to menu/button presses.
Audio/video demonstration: play low, mid, and high keys (at least one octave each) with audible output.
Crackle check: sustained notes/chords and a short stop/start segment.
Clear photo/video of the adapter (label/spec + connector) or show it powering the keyboard.
Close-up photos of any scuffed/damaged areas on the control panel and speaker grille.
response.reason: Even though the seller asserts they tested it, there is still no remote evidence (no power-on screen, no audio/key/button demonstration, and no adapter shown). Without that, the 'working perfectly/no crackle' claims remain unverified, so pricing should wait for proof.
